title: Non-blocking findings from PR #296's review (round-timestamp fix: evidence wording and instruction placement)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #296 (backend-closed-trades-legacy-exit-reason-500-followups-followups-followups), which added a real date -u timestamp-capture reminder to .claude/agents/task-worker.md step 5 and left the already-done parent task's round timestamps untouched. The PR itself is accepted -- full backend suite passed (1203 passed, 100% coverage), frontend suite passed (841 passed, 99.7%+ coverage), ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc and the profit-target wording guard were all clean, scripts/validate_tasks.py and its own unittest suite (41 tests) passed, and an independent code-review pass found zero correctness issues. These two findings are wording/placement nits only.

checklist.step: The second decisions entry's supporting grep evidence says an exact T00:00:00Z timestamp appears on 'dozens of distinct dates each with 20-50+ entries apiece' to justify skipping a validate_tasks.py round-timestamp check. Re-running the same grep confirms there are 13 distinct dates with this exact pattern (roughly matching 'dozens'), but only 6 of those 13 actually have >=20 entries -- the other 7 range from 2 to 14 (2026-09-24: 2, 2026-09-14: 4, 2026-09-23: 5, 2026-09-13: 11, 2026-09-21: 12, 2026-09-12/2026-09-15: 13 each, 2026-09-18: 14). The underlying conclusion (this pattern is pervasive enough board-wide that a validator check would produce heavy false-positive noise) still holds even with the more accurate per-date range, so this doesn't change the decision -- but the '20-50+ entries apiece' phrasing overstates the evidence for roughly half the dates cited. Worth a follow-up decisions-entry note (or a corrected re-statement) giving the accurate per-date range if this evidence is ever cited again.

task-worker.md's new timestamping instruction is written generically enough ('or any other timestamp you write into a task JSON -- git.pushed_at included') to also cover the questions[].timestamp field task-worker writes in its own step 6, but it's placed entirely within step 5's discussion of decisions entries with no cross-reference from step 6 (which still shows a bare '{"timestamp": "<ISO 8601 UTC>", ...}' example with no reminder to actually capture it via date -u). A future reader skimming step 6 in isolation could miss that the step 5 rule applies there too. Consider either a short cross-reference from step 6 back to step 5's rule, or moving the timestamping rule to a standalone bullet that isn't scoped under one specific step, so it's unambiguously read as applying to every timestamp task-worker writes.

decisions.decision: Corrected the wording of `backend-closed-trades-legacy-exit-reason-500-followups-followups-followups.json`'s second `decisions` entry in place (narrow carve-out applies: this checklist item explicitly names that entry's own text as the thing to fix). Replaced 'shows dozens of distinct dates each with 20-50+ entries apiece' with the accurate per-date breakdown: 13 distinct dates total, only 5 with >=20 entries (50, 48, 47, 34, 23), the remaining 8 ranging from 2 to 14. While re-verifying the grep myself to write the corrected text, found the checklist item's own '6 of those 13' figure is itself off by one -- the actual count of dates with >=20 entries is 5, not 6 (matching PR #296's `pr_decision.notes`, which had already flagged this exact discrepancy: 'its own re-count claims 6 of 13 dates have >=20 entries, but recomputing gives 5 (50/48/47/34/23)'). Used the verified-correct figure (5) in the actual edit rather than propagating the checklist item's '6' into the done task's decisions entry, since the point of this task is accuracy, not reproducing an already-flagged miscount.
decisions.rationale: The `pr_decision.notes` on the parent-of-parent task already did the work of re-running the grep and catching this exact off-by-one, and explicitly left it for 'a future pass on the follow-up task' to fix the count -- this is that pass. Propagating '6' into the corrected decisions-entry text would have replaced one overstated figure with a different, still-wrong one, defeating the purpose of the correction; re-verifying against a fresh `grep -rhoE '"timestamp": *"[^"]+"' docs/tasks/*.json docs/tasks/done/*.json | grep 'T00:00:00Z' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` (run directly, not trusted from memory) confirmed 5 is correct. The underlying conclusion (pervasive enough to make a validator check noisy) is unaffected either way, so this doesn't reopen any substantive decision -- it's the same kind of narrow factual correction the checklist item itself calls for, just carried one step further with fresher evidence.

decisions.decision: For task-worker.md step 6, added a short cross-reference back to step 5's date -u timestamp-capture rule directly at the point step 6 introduces its own `questions[].timestamp` field, rather than moving the rule out to a standalone bullet.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item offered either option ('a short cross-reference from step 6 back to step 5's rule, or moving the timestamping rule to a standalone bullet'). The cross-reference is the smaller, more surgical diff: step 5 is still the natural home for the rule since it's where the concept (and the concrete `decisions`-entry example) is first introduced, and step 6 only needs a pointer at the exact spot a reader would otherwise miss it (the `questions` entry's own `timestamp` field) rather than a structural reorganization of the whole numbered list. Promoting it to a standalone bullet would require renumbering-adjacent surrounding prose for no added clarity, since every current and future timestamp-writing step can just point back to the one canonical rule.
